after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series
 

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}.
$$
after.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{2n+3}}{(2n+3)!}\cdot \frac{(2n+1)!}{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1){x}^{2}}{(2n+3)(2n+2)}| \\  & =|-{x}^{2}|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(2n+3)(2n+2)} \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty ,$ and the interval of convergence is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(\frac{x}{n})}^{n}\,.
$$
after.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{n}}{{n}^{n}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{(n+1)^{n+1}}\cdot \frac{{n}^{n}}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{x{n}^{n}}{(n+1)^{n+1}}| \\  & =|x|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{n}^{n}}{(n+1)^{n+1}} \\  & =|x|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n+1}{(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{n} \\  & =|x|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n+1}{(1+\frac{1}{n})}^{-n} \\  & =|x|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{e(n+1)} \\  & =|x|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty ,$ and the interval of convergence is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)}=\frac{x}{2\cdot 2}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{2}^{2}\cdot 5}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{{2}^{3}\cdot 8}+⋯\,.
$$
after.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{2}^{n+1}(3n+2)}\cdot \frac{{2}^{n}(3n-1)}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{x(3n-1)}{2(3n+2)}| \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{3n-1}{3n+2} \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{|x|}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{|x|}{2}<1\,⟹\,|x|<2.
$$

So, the radius of convergence is $2,$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(-2,2).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x|=2,$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=-2$ and $x=2$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{2}^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{3n-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{8}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To see if this series converges, we use the limit comparision test, whith ${a}_{n}=\frac{1}{3n-1}$ and ${b}_{n}=\frac{1}{n}.$ We observe that ${a}_{n}$ and ${b}_{n}$ are positive, and

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{a}_{n}}{{b}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{3n-1})}{(\frac{1}{n})}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{n}{3n-1}=\frac{1}{3},
$$

 
which is positive and finite. Hence, the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ and ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ either *both* converge or *both* diverge.
Since ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n}$ is divergent, the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{3n-1}$ is also divergent by the limit comparison test. So the endpoint $x=2$ is not included in our interval.

- When $x=-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-2)^{n}}{{2}^{n}(3n-1)} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{3n-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{8}+⋯,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the alternating series test. So the endpoint $x=-2$ is included in our interval.

Therefore, the interval of convergence is $[-2,2).$
